result: The authors developed WNet3D, a novel self-supervised 3D segmentation model adapted from WNet, with architectural modifications including conversion to fully 3D architecture, use of SoftNCuts loss, group normalization, and reduced model complexity for improved performance.

result: On the mesoSPIM dataset, WNet3D achieves performance comparable to or better than supervised methods (Cellpose, StarDist, SwinUNetR, SegResNet) without requiring labeled training data, with F1-scores of 0.74-0.81 depending on filtering, and shows particular advantages in low-data regimes.

result: A SwinUNetR model trained using WNet3D-generated pseudo-labels achieves performance nearly equivalent to a fully supervised model trained on human annotations, demonstrating the feasibility of active learning approaches.

result: The pretrained WNet3D model, trained only on mesoSPIM data, generalizes well to three diverse external datasets (Platynereis-ISH-Nuclei, Platynereis-Nuclei, Mouse-Skull-Nuclei) with different imaging modalities, achieving the highest average F1-Score on each dataset.
